findings.claim: A memoized seeded:false snapshot could overwrite state seeded by another process.
findings.evidence: Gemini identified the race; the new cross-instance regression failed when the re-read was removed and passes on HEAD.

findings.claim: A rejected initPromise permanently prevented initialization retry.
findings.evidence: The retry regression failed when initPromise reset was removed and passes on HEAD in both adapters.

findings.claim: Direct file saves could leave a truncated snapshot after process failure.
findings.evidence: filePersistence.save now writes, fsyncs, atomically renames, and removes its temporary file; core tests pass.

findings.claim: prepareSeed discarded newly generated keys when restored descriptors were non-empty.
findings.evidence: The restored-plus-new App regression failed when the merge loop was removed and passes on HEAD.

findings.claim: After a cross-process canonical re-read, later mutating saves reused stale generatedSecrets metadata.
findings.evidence: Claude Haiku identified the stale preparation cache; both adapters now replace preparationPromise with the canonical prepared state, and the metadata regression fails when that assignment is removed.

findings.claim: A rejected preparationPromise permanently prevented retry after a transient persistence.initialize failure.
findings.evidence: Cursor Grok 4.6 identified the rejected cache; both adapters now clear only the still-current failed promise, and both regression tests went red without the fix and green after restoration.

findings.claim: The save-failure retry regression did not prove generated identity stability.
findings.evidence: Cursor Grok 4.6 identified the weak oracle; both tests now persist initialization state, authenticate retries with the original JWT, and assert generatedSecrets remains unchanged.
findings.path: generatedSecrets -> failed enqueueSave -> request retry -> JWT auth
